title: Patrol Y62 / Armada
verdict: The Y62 traded the Patrol's live axles for a 5.6-litre V8, independent suspension and a clever hydraulic anti-roll system, and the Gulf loved it for it. Americans got the same truck as the Armada, minus the locker and the clever bits, which makes it the most capable family hauler nobody takes off-road.

paragraphs: Nissan launched the sixth-generation Patrol, the Y62, in Abu Dhabi on 13 February 2010, which tells you who it was built for. It broke with six decades of Patrol tradition. The [[nissan-patrol/y61|Y61]] it replaced kept solid axles at both ends, as had every Patrol before it, from the leaf-sprung [[nissan-patrol/160-mq|160/MQ]] to the coil-sprung [[nissan-patrol/y60|Y60]]. The Y62 got independent suspension at all four corners, a direct-injection 5.6-litre V8 and an optional hydraulic system whose rams do the work of both dampers and anti-roll bars. In North America the same truck became the Infiniti QX56 in 2010 and the Nissan Armada for 2017–2024.

story.heading: A V8 AND FOUR INDEPENDENT CORNERS
paragraphs: The engine is the VK56VD, rated at 298 kW at 5,800 rpm and 560 Nm at 4,000 rpm in the Patrol, according to 4X4 Australia. Wikipedia says entry-level trims first used a 236 kW VK56DE V8 and, from 2017, a 4.0-litre VQ40DE V6 with 205 kW. All models have had a seven-speed automatic since 2017. Early entry trims offered a five-speed automatic or a six-speed manual. There's no diesel, which South Africa's Cars.co.za lists as one of the truck's weaknesses.

Underneath is a separate frame with a two-speed transfer case. Patrolapart describes the Y62's 4WD as an electronic multi-plate clutch unit that needs Nissan's ATX 90A fluid. The driver picks Auto, 4H or 4L, plus Sand, Rock and Snow modes. Non-US trucks have a rear differential lock and hill descent control, and Cars.co.za lists a helical limited-slip rear diff as well. 4X4 Australia's tester praised the wheel travel, low range and traction control, and grumbled that the traction control switches off when the rear locker is engaged.

story.heading: HYDRAULIC BODY MOTION CONTROL
paragraphs: HBMC is the Y62's party trick. Nissan's description: the hydraulic cylinders at each wheel are cross-linked by pipes in two circuits, so when the truck leans into a corner, fluid from the outside cylinders flows into an accumulator and raises roll stiffness. Off-road, each wheel is free to rise or drop with the ground. Nissan says it needs no power source, so it costs nothing in fuel. 4X4 Australia puts it more simply: the rams act as both the shock absorbers and the sway bars. Wikipedia says Nissan developed it and tested it on the Patrol in the Middle East.

The catch arrives when you want to lift it. On NissanPatrol.com.au, one owner's research found that HBMC front springs can't be swapped on their own, only as complete shock-and-spring units, and another watched his rear end sink three inches under 280 kg of ball weight. Ontrack's 2-inch lift kits for HBMC trucks are designed to fit without disturbing the system's pressure. When Nissan Australia and Premcar built the 2023 Patrol Warrior, they kept HBMC and re-valved it. Not every Y62 has it: Wikipedia says the Gulf-market Desert Edition used conventional suspension, and the US Armada never offered it.

story.heading: BUILT FOR THE GULF
paragraphs: The Y62 went on sale in Dubai on 1 April 2010. By mid-May, dealer Arabian Automobiles had delivered more than 450 and was taking desert-safari operators dune-bashing in them. Nissan claimed more than 13,000 hours of testing in local deserts. It paid off. In The National's 2013 report, Nissan Middle East said Patrol sales had grown 66 per cent in a year, to more than 14,000 across the region, giving it 22 per cent of the Gulf SUV segment.

The love has lasted. Bestselling Cars Blog reports the Patrol was the UAE's best-selling vehicle of 2024, its first win since 2020. Gulf Business's 2024 interview with Nissan's Middle East chief calls it 'a cultural symbol'. Gulf buyers got grades from XE to LE Platinum City, plus a Nismo with 319 kW, Bilstein dampers and 22-inch forged wheels, launched in Dubai. Japan, oddly, never got the Y62 new. Wikipedia says it was export-only, and most Y62s in Japan are reverse-imported US Armadas.

story.heading: THE ARMADA YEARS AND WHAT CAME NEXT
paragraphs: Nissan showed the second-generation Armada in Chicago in 2016, and it went on sale that August as a 2017 model, built in Kyushu alongside the Patrol. It had a 390 hp VK56VD and a seven-speed automatic, and a 2021 refresh added 10 hp and 19 lb-ft. AutoGuide reported that US buyers didn't get the Patrol's locking differentials, disconnecting sway bars or HBMC, and that the US truck had its own suspension tuning. What it kept was the frame, low range and 8,500 lb of towing. It was the first Patrol-based Nissan sold in America since the [[nissan-patrol/patrol-60|60 Series]] left in 1969.

The Y62 had a 2014 facelift, a heavier one in 2019 (the Armada's came for 2021) and limited editions such as the 2021 Middle East 70th Anniversary. Australia got the Warrior in 2023, with a 50 mm lift, 295/70R18 Yokohama all-terrains and 323 mm of ground clearance. Its successor, the Y63, was unveiled in Abu Dhabi on 3 September 2024 with V6 engines, including a 425 hp twin-turbo, and a nine-speed automatic. Its Armada twin went on sale in the US that December. Wikipedia says the Y63 reaches Australia in November 2026, so the Y62 is still on sale in some markets as this is written.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · ARMADA VS PATROL
callout.title: Same truck, different toolkit
paragraphs: Under the skin, the 2017–2024 Armada is a Y62. Autoblog called it the same 'rugged body-on-frame chassis and powertrain' the rest of the world calls the Patrol. AutoGuide listed what was left out for the US: front and rear locking differentials, the disconnecting sway bars and HBMC. The US truck got unique suspension tuning and just over 9 inches of ground clearance instead.

So an Armada is a Patrol with an open rear diff and conventional sway bars. That makes it the easiest Y62 to buy and the hardest to turn into a desert truck. Only the next generation, the Y63, brought an Armada Pro-4X with an electronic locking differential and air suspension.

engineering_intro: The Y62 is still a body-on-frame truck with a real low range, but it's the first Patrol with independent suspension at both ends. The big V8, the seven-speed automatic and a clutch-type transfer case are shared across the Patrol, Armada and Infiniti QX56/QX80. The rear locker and the HBMC hydraulics are what separate a Gulf or Australian Patrol from a US Armada.

buying_checks.head: Shift quality
buying_checks.body: CarSwitch says the RE7R01A seven-speed in early Y62s (2010–2014) has a reputation for valve-body problems, costing AED 5,000–12,000 to fix in the UAE. Test for harsh shifts, delayed engagement and shudder between second and third. One Australian owner reported his Y62 holding gears under hard acceleration while towing, even after a warranty transmission.

buying_checks.head: Signs of a hard desert life
buying_checks.body: CarSwitch's desert checklist: gouged skid plates and crossmembers, compacted sand in the frame rails and behind the inner guard liners, fine sand in the air filter, and ABS, stability or TPMS warnings on a cold start.

buying_checks.head: Patrol or Armada?
buying_checks.body: A US Armada has no rear locker, no disconnecting sway bars and no HBMC (AutoGuide). If you want a locker, you're shopping for a Patrol, and a Y62 Patrol isn't old enough to import into the US under the 25-year rule.

buying_checks.head: HBMC and lift kits
buying_checks.body: If the truck has HBMC, ask what's been done to it. One owner found HBMC front springs only come as complete shock-and-spring assemblies, and HBMC-specific kits such as Ontrack's are designed to fit without disturbing the system. Look for wet hydraulic lines and fittings at each corner and a truck that sits level.

buying_checks.head: Modifications and warranty
buying_checks.body: Cars.co.za advises avoiding heavily modified examples. One NissanPatrol.com.au member was told by his dealer that drivetrain problems wouldn't be covered after a lift.

buying_checks.head: Towing history
buying_checks.body: Owners report the rear of an HBMC truck sagging under heavy ball weights. Many towing rigs have airbag kits designed for HBMC. A transmission cooler or deep pan is a good sign on a truck that has towed.

buying_checks.head: Armada recalls
buying_checks.body: Check the VIN with NHTSA. The 2020–2021 Armada fuel-pump recall (21V373) replaces a pump whose impeller can swell and stall the engine. The 2026 campaign 26V455 corrects the axle-weight label on Armadas with 22-inch wheels.

buying_checks.head: Brakes and tyres
buying_checks.body: It's a heavy truck (a Warrior weighs 2,884 kg). Cars.co.za notes the weight wears brakes and tyres quickly, so check pad and rotor thickness and tyre wear before you price the truck.

repairs.title: Automatic transmission fluid and filter service
repairs.symptoms: Harsh or late shifts, flare between gears, or fluid that's dark and smells burnt, especially on a truck that tows.
repairs.fix: The RE7 seven-speed uses Nissan Matic-S fluid and has its filter inside the pan. Drain the fluid, drop the pan, replace the filter and pan gasket, clean the pan and refit it. Refill with Matic-S through the fill plug and set the level using the procedure in the workshop manual, which depends on fluid temperature [CONFIRM PROCEDURE IN MANUAL]. Owners who tow often fit a deeper cast pan (Patrolapart's adds 3 L) and an auxiliary cooler.
repairs.tools: Socket set · drain tray · fluid pump · scan tool or thermometer for fluid temperature · torque wrench

repairs.title: Fit an auxiliary transmission cooler
repairs.symptoms: High transmission temperatures when towing, climbing or crawling in sand.
repairs.fix: Mount the cooler core ahead of the radiator using the kit's brackets, route the supplied hoses into the transmission cooler circuit, and clamp everything clear of the fan and exhaust. Top up the fluid afterwards. The kit's maker suggests adding about 1 L of full-synthetic fluid. Run the engine, check for leaks and recheck the level.
repairs.tools: Socket set · hose cutter · clamps · drip tray

repairs.title: Brake pads and rotors
repairs.symptoms: Squealing or grinding, a brake warning light, pedal pulsation, or stopping that feels weak under load.
repairs.fix: Support the truck, remove the wheels, unbolt the caliper and carrier, and hang the caliper so the hose isn't stretched. Fit new rotors and pads with the supplied shims and hardware. Clean and grease the slide pins, push the pistons back carefully, torque the carrier and caliper bolts to the manual, then bed the pads in. Genuine Nissan front and rear kits each come with four pads.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands · caliper piston tool · torque wrench · brake cleaner

repairs.title: No-start: brake light switch
repairs.symptoms: The push-button start won't crank the engine, often along with brake lights that don't work.
repairs.fix: With push-button start, the truck needs a signal that the brake pedal is pressed before it will start. Patrolapart says that signal comes from the brake light switch on the pedal assembly. Check the brake lights first. If they don't work and the truck won't start, unplug the switch at the pedal, remove it, fit the new one and set its adjustment to the manual before reconnecting.

parts.name: Brake light pedal switch (car won't start), Y62 VK56

repairs.title: Front wheel hub and bearing
repairs.symptoms: A hum or grinding that rises with road speed, vibration through the wheel, or an ABS light.
repairs.fix: The Y62's front bearing comes as a hub assembly with the bearing pre-greased and the ABS speed sensor attached. Patrolapart's unit fits either side. Remove the wheel, caliper and rotor and the axle nut, unplug the ABS sensor, unbolt the hub from the knuckle and fit the new assembly. Torque the hub bolts and axle nut to the manual.
repairs.tools: Axle nut socket · breaker bar · torque wrench · puller if the hub is seized

parts.name: Left or right front wheel hub assembly, Y62

repairs.title: Serpentine belt and tensioner
repairs.symptoms: Squeal from the front of the engine, a vibrating belt, or a cracked or glazed belt.
repairs.fix: Note the belt routing before you start. Rotate the automatic tensioner to release the tension and remove the belt. Check the tensioner and idlers for noise and wobble, and replace the tensioner if it's weak. The belt drives the alternator, power steering pump and A/C compressor, so a failure can mean losing power steering and charging. Fit the new belt and release the tensioner slowly.
repairs.tools: Long-handled ratchet or belt tool · torch

repairs.title: Thermostat and water pump
repairs.symptoms: Overheating, an engine that runs cold, an erratic temperature gauge, or coolant weeping from the front of the engine.
repairs.fix: Know your series first. Patrolapart lists an 82°C thermostat that needs no gasket for Series 1 and 2 trucks, and an electronically controlled thermostat assembly for Series 3 trucks from February 2016. Drain the coolant, replace the thermostat (and the water pump and its separate gasket, if it's leaking or noisy), refill with Nissan blue long-life coolant and bleed the system.
repairs.tools: Socket set · drain tray · coolant funnel · torque wrench

repairs.title: Front inner CV boot
repairs.symptoms: Grease flung around the inside of the wheel or on the suspension, or a clicking CV joint on full lock.
repairs.fix: Replace a split boot before dirt gets into the joint. Remove the driveshaft from the hub and diff, cut off the old boot, clean out the old grease, pack the joint with the sachet of CV grease supplied, and fit the new boot and clamps. Patrolapart says lifted trucks put extra strain on the boots.
repairs.tools: Axle nut socket · CV clamp pliers · circlip pliers · torque wrench

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: We couldn't find a solid owner consensus for a stock Y62. Stock is 265/70R18 on Australian Patrols and the Armada SV, or 275/60R20 on higher grades. 6061 Works lists 275/70R18 as a mild upgrade, about 15 mm taller than stock. For 295/70R18, Nissan's own Warrior needed a 29 mm suspension lift, and 6061 Works recommends that size after a 2-inch lift. Nissan sells re-gear sets for trucks on 35s.

faq.q: Is the Armada the same truck as the Patrol?
faq.a: The 2017–2024 Armada shares the Y62's frame and powertrain and is built alongside it in Japan. AutoGuide reported that the US version lacked the Patrol's locking differentials, disconnecting sway bars and HBMC, and had its own suspension tuning.

faq.q: Can I import a Y62 Patrol into the US?
faq.a: Not yet, unless it was built to US standards. NHTSA's 25-year exemption counts from the date of manufacture, so the earliest 2010 Y62 Patrols become eligible around 2035. Until then the Armada is the US-legal Y62.

faq.q: What is HBMC, and does it stop me lifting the truck?
faq.a: Hydraulic Body Motion Control cross-links hydraulic rams at each wheel through accumulators, so they act as both dampers and anti-roll bars. You can lift an HBMC truck, but you need a kit designed for it. One owner says HBMC front springs only come as complete assemblies, and Ontrack's 2-inch kits are designed to keep the system's pressure intact.

faq.q: Which years should I buy or avoid?
faq.a: CarSwitch, a UAE used-car marketplace, rates 2015–2017 trucks as the value sweet spot and the 2020–2021 facelifts as the best recent buys. Perth dealer Westside Auto calls the 2020-on facelift Patrols the most desirable on the used market. CarSwitch suggests caution with 2010–2012 trucks because of transmission valve-body problems and early fit-and-finish issues. In the US, run any 2020–2021 Armada's VIN for the fuel-pump recall.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: The EPA rates every 2017–2024 Armada 4WD at 13 mpg city, 18 highway and 15 combined. In Australia the official Patrol figure is 14.4 L/100 km, and 4X4 Australia averaged 15.2 L/100 km on test, or about 12 to 13 on the freeway.

3,500 kg braked for the Patrol (Cars.co.za, 4X4 Australia) and 8,500 lb for the 2017 Armada (AutoGuide). Owners of HBMC trucks report rear sag under heavy ball weights, and airbag kits are made specifically for HBMC suspension.
The EPA lists regular fuel for 2017–2020 Armadas and premium for the 2021–2024 trucks with the 400 hp tune.
No. The Y62 was sold with petrol V8s and, in some markets, a 4.0 V6. Cars.co.za lists the lack of a turbo-diesel among its weaknesses.

faq.q: What transmission fluid does it take?
faq.a: Nissan Matic-S in the seven-speed automatic, and Nissan ATX 90A in the transfer case. Patrolapart gives the transfer-case service refill as 1.5 litres.

The Y63 Patrol, unveiled in Abu Dhabi on 3 September 2024, with a 3.8 V6 or a 3.5 twin-turbo V6 (425 hp, 700 Nm) and a nine-speed automatic. The matching Armada went on sale in the US in December 2024, and Wikipedia says Australia gets the Y63 in November 2026.

baseline_service.intro: A used Y62 has usually done one of three jobs: school runs, desert weekends or towing a caravan across Australia. Baseline everything, and pay special attention to the transmission and transfer-case fluids, which are model-specific. The oil, plug, diff and brake-fluid specs below are from Nissan USA's owner's manuals for the Armada, the US-market Y62. Patrols sold elsewhere may specify different grades, so check your own manual.
